problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨{t}^{2}-6t,(t-3)^{5}⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=\pi .$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=\pi ,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\pi ) & =⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨-4,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=\pi $ we calculate the magnitude of $v(\pi ),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(\pi )| & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+0} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed when $t=\pi $ is $4.$
